newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end higher, boosted by blue chip buys.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end higher, boosted by blue chip buys.

text.p: Shares closed Tuesday's trading higher after investors put the spotlight on major blue chips, with Samsung Electronics and Korea Electric Power leading the way, brokers said. The index rose 8.71 points to provisionally close at 777.91, while 26.66 million shares changed hands.
Brokers said investors were preparing for the expansion of the foreign shareholdings ceiling on October 1, when it will be raised to 20 percent for most stocks from 18 percet.
"Large-caps were well sustained today because domestic investors think these stocks are preferred by foreigners," said a Dongsuh Securities broker.
Samsung climbed 1,300 won, or 2.21 percent, to 60,200, while KEPCO rose 700 won, or 2.59 percent, to 27,700. Both are expected to be targets of foreign buying when limits are eased.

Brokers said that the market was expected to continue to rise steadily ahead of next Tuesday. But margin loan pressures and uncertainty about the level of foreign investors' enthusiasm for the stock market would stop the bourse from sharp rises.

Small-cap shares also outperformed the market. Domestic investors unnerved by the slowdown of economic growth were planning to sell large manufacturers to foreigners and move into smaller, domestic demand-oriented stocks, brokers said.
